steps.text: There was a fire at a residential building downtown.

steps.name: Shaw
steps.text: Everyone, don'tpanic! Pleasefollowourinstructions andevacuatetooutside thecordonedoffarea. Donotpanic...
It's gone... My life savings... all gone...
Hahaha... That's what I'm talking about! Burn this whole stinking place to the ground! Hahahaha...

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Clear a path! Use triage! Care for the heavily injured first!

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Chief, no sign of anyone still trapped.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Everyone, please take a look around and see if there's anyone you know who hasn't evacuated?

steps.name: Female Resident
steps.text: Has anyone seen the weird guy who lives on the second floor...?

steps.name: Male Resident
steps.text: Right, now that you mention it, I don't think I've seen him.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: The second floor? Isn't that where the fire started?

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: That doesn’t sound good. Do you know if he's home?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: He leaves his blinds open every time he goes out, but his blinds were closed when I came down the stairs just now.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Tell HQ! There's someone trapped inside. The fire has grown so big that the firefighters can't go back in. Send fire trucks. Right now—

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: The fire’s probably from an Originium fire starter explosion. It might set off a chain reaction any minutet—

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Stay in contact... and be careful.

steps.name: Comms
steps.text: Shaw, how’s it going in there...?

steps.name: Comms
steps.text: Shaw, give me a status report.

steps.name: Comms
steps.text: Shaw, don't push yourself. If you can't get inside, come back down right away!
The tiny Zalak slams on the burning hot steel door with her shoulder. It doesn't bulge.
Sparks fly everywhere. Shaw's axe turns scalding hot from the heat of the fire.
She tightly grips her axe's handle and slams it toward the door's lock. The fissure on the lock is already clear.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: You scared the hell out of me. I’m glad you’re awake...

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: And don't worry. The fire's out. You did great.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: But now I’m worried about you. The medic says you breathed in a little too much carbon monoxide. You need to get some rest.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Don't move too much, and keep your oxygen mask on.

steps.name: Shaw
steps.text: Oh, wait! Whataboutthatguy?! Whathappened totheguywhowastrapped inthebuilding?! Igotta—
Shaw never expected to find such a small room behind the door.
Everything inside has been burned to ashes, which in turn makes the room look that much more open.
There is a safe in the corner of the room. Although warped from the heat, its contents are miraculously intact.
A small stack of LMD bills and a stamp album.
The fire erupted so quickly. In the end, one person died, with eleven in critical condition.
That was the first time I saw a life extinguished right before my eyes.
I got distracted during training; got reprimanded. Had to write a self-reflection report.

The investigation into the fire the other day has wrapped up. It was started by a worn-out home-use Originium fire starter device, which set off a chain of explosions. The residents had too many things strewn around the building, which helped the fire spread.
I was commended at the ceremony today.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Right. You were there yourself. His whole life was burned to a crisp. There weren't any clues for us to work with.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: We asked around in the neighborhood. All we learned is that the deceased was a single male. No idea what he did for a living or what his relationships were like.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: We put a notice in the papers asking anyone to come forward to claim his remains. We still haven't heard from anyone.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: That's not something we have to worry about.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Oh, that thing, huh? We looked into it.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: No idea why he kept it in the safe, but analysis shows it's just a normal stamp album. There aren't even any fingerprints. We couldn't find any leads at all.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Why are you still asking about the fire, Shaw? The investigation must be over by now.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: It was a home-use Originium fire starter that burned the place down. Both the L.G.D. and fire department arrived at that conclusion. There's nothing suspicious about it.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: If we go by the book, we're supposed to destroy all personal effects left behind by nameless victims. I could give it to you, but what for?

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: *Sigh*, what do I do with you... Come with me.

steps.name: Male Resident
steps.text: The guy who lived on the second floor? Didn't you ask me just a couple days ago? I didn't know him!

steps.name: Male Resident
steps.text: Every time I had to see that shitty face of his, it was all I could do to keep from punching it in. He never gave anyone the time of day. Why would we care about him?

steps.name: Male Resident
steps.text: Look, half my flat got burned down. I don't have the time to worry about some guy. I'm busy. Now leave me alone.

steps.name: Female Resident
steps.text: There aren’t many of us in this building, so we all know each other, more or less...

steps.name: Female Resident
steps.text: But that guy never talked to anyone. He never left his room during the day, either, so nobody knew much about him...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I met that uncle once. He was really big! He was like thiiiiiis tall!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: He smiled at me and gave me a candy, too!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Huh? Was he an uncle or a grandpa? I'm not too sure...

steps.name: Female Resident
steps.text: Mio! How many times have I told you not to accept things from strangers?!

steps.name: Female Resident
steps.text: I'm sorry, we can't help you. We have some errands to run. Bye now.
I talked to a lot of people, but no one knew anything about the man.
It was like the fire burned away every trace of his life, like he never existed at all.
No, this isn't in my job description. I can't write about this here...

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: Oh? If you want an appraisal on your collectibles, you need to make a reservation with the postal collectible specialists, and I'm about to clock out...

steps.name: Shaw
steps.text: No, that'snotit! I'mverysorry, Ijustwantedtoask, wouldyoubeable totellanythingaboutitsowner justbylooking atthestampalbum?

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: What do you mean by that... It's not yours?

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: Alright, alright. Slow down. Hand it over.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: Hm... You don't see a collection like this very often.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: Not really. It's just strange. Why would someone collect stamps like this?

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: When people collect stamps, they’re usually either limited edition stamps or stamps that have some special significance, right?

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: But the stamps in here are all very common. There's no value in it whatsoever.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: I can't tell you what the collector was thinking. The stamps' themes and years are all jumbled up, and he kept both postmarked and non-postmarked stamps together...

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: A lot of it has Kou-wu landscapes, though. Look, from this page onwards, it's all Kou-wu sceneries.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: Now this 'Hui-ch'i Foothills' one is a classic. If my memory serves, it was issued a couple decades ago? They printed a lot of them, though, so it's not worth that much money.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: That aside, I couldn’t tell you what's so special about this collection.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: If you wanted to learn something about the owner from the collection, I'm afraid there's not much.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: If I had to give you an answer, maybe he likes the landscapes in Kou-wu?

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Come in, come in. Take a seat anywhere.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: What? Girl, go ahead and ask every restaurant in Lungmen. See if anyone dares to say they serve more authentic Kou-wunese food than me?!

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: People from Kou-wu? Of course. We've served many Kou-wunese expats here. All of them say our food takes them right back home.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: If you don't believe me, why don’t you try it yourself?

steps.name: Shaw
steps.text: He... HewasprobablyKou-wuese... Areallytallman, andprobablykindofhardup. Heprobablylookedalittleangry... maybenot... buthewouldcomefodinner intheevenings, otherwisealwayskeepingtohimself...

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: You said... it was a tall guy?

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: That rings a bell... Yes, it does. There's a customer like that.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Yeah... He’s a regular, sort of.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: It's just like you said. He always comes by himself, and always around midnight just before closing. I always have to stick around an extra hour for him.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: He never orders much, either. Just a finbeast and a small side dish. A thing of liquor, too. He hangs around a little after he's done before heading on home.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Yeah, he looks real scary, but he's not a bad fella. Helps me clean up once he's done, too. Sometimes he talks about home when he's had a little too much to drink.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Friends or family? He never told me about them, but he certainly doesn't seem like he's married.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: If you want to know, I could ask him for you next time? Wait, no, this is a customer's privacy we're talking about... *Sigh*... You'll just have to ask him yourself.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Won't be back again? No way. He loves my food. He's one of the ones I was talking about, always saying my cooking reminds them of home.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: You're right, though. I haven’t seen him in a while...

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: I wonder what that young man's been up to.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Right, he's a young man. Maybe a little older than you, but probably not by much.

steps.name: Post Office Worker
steps.text: Now this 'Hui-ch'i Foothills' one is a classic. If my memory serves, it was issued a couple decades ago?

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Hey, hey now, girl. Why are you crying, all of a sudden? A-Are you looking for family?

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: A-Alright, the next time he shows up, I'll ask him every last detail. Don't cry, okay?

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: Hey, speak of the devil. Now you pop in, eh, kid? Look at this girl, she's been asking after you, even started crying.

steps.name: Restaurant Owner
steps.text: I have no idea what's going on, but help me out here.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: 'Hui-ch'i Foothills...' I grew up in a small town at the base of Mount Hui-ch'i. A place just like this.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: I even remember this small pond behind the mountain. All the finbeasts we ate when I was a kid were from there.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: You can buy the freshest fins at the docks here, but there aren't any great fincatching spots like that pond.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: It's been years since I've been home, but the place still looks just as lovely as always, at least on these stamps.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Kou-wu isn't a big place, and there's not that many people there either. But, I can’t say I know him.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: That said, now that you told me all this, I guess he doesn't feel a total stranger to me anymore. What a thorough girl you are, though. Not even we were this meticulous in our investigation.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Hard to say... but he was probably homesick.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: So you took the stamp album because you wanted to find his family?

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Why are you so obsessed with him?

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Shaw, I'll say this no matter how many times it takes. You've done your job. Under those circumstances, no one could've done better, not even you yourself.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: I can't tell you that's a wrong way to think, but with this kind of baggage, can you really throw yourself into the next fire without hesitating?

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Alright, I've said enough. This is something you have to figure out. I’m in no position to lecture you.

steps.name: Senior L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: It's chilly tonight. Head home soon.
Today's the last day of my vacation. I did something really embarrassing.
In the end, I couldn't find anything about the man. I don't know what to do to pull myself together, but I still have more important work.
Today's my first day back on the job.
I've fallen behind on my training, so I gotta catch up. I might've caught a cold, and I need to get better!

steps.name: Shaw
steps.text: Wemustalwayskeepinmind howtoproperlyescape thesceneofafire, butintheend, themosteffectivewaytofightfires isbypreventingthemfromhappening inthefirstplace.

steps.name: Shaw
steps.text: UnlikeCatastrophes, it'susuallypeople whostartfires, butittakesmorethan ourwillpoweralone tostopfires.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Hey, Skyfire. Is it just me or did the squirt sound like she was kinda nervous that whole talk?

steps.name: Skyfire
steps.text: Shh—Listen to her. She's telling this to you, specifically. Now stop interrupting!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: As if she doesn’t mean you—

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Still, she looks kinda sad, though. What should we do? Cheer her up, maybe?
